dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Twenty years ago, the Akademiya had just received Sachin's estate. To celebrate the huge investment, the Akademiya Extravaganza that year was grander than usual.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I was very young then, and I remember seeing posters for the Interdarshan Championship all over the city. I couldn't help but mention it to my father. I even told him that I really liked the look of the diadem — it was so unique.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: So he said, "Why don't I win it, so I can let you play with it for a few days?"

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: That made me very happy, and I nodded enthusiastically. But to my surprise, he didn't win, and when he got back home, he seemed extremely depressed.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Later, he left home, saying that he wanted to do some investigating in the desert... The quicksand got him not long after that...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...For many years, I couldn't face up to it at all. If I'd just kept my mouth shut, maybe none of it would have ever happened.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Where were you while the rest of us were eating together?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I don't recall being obligated to report my whereabouts to you.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Did you go find another hidey-hole to read in? You need to change your ways, you know. You can't survive on books alone.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Surviving on meals paid for by you would be harder still.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You...!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Hmph, whatever, it doesn't take a genius to guess what you've been up to... You were investigating Sachin, weren't you? It was obvious from your notes. However, I don't believe his research alone would've been enough to pique your interest.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: His way of doing things is disturbing, while you... Well, to be fair, your philosophy disgusts me too, but you and Sachin are nothing alike. I don't imagine your views intersect at all. Egoism and nihilism are not the same thing.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: My personal interest aside, Sachin's legacy is not entirely meaningless — he conducted experiments on a great scale, and left his findings behind.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Also, thanks for the compliment. But I'm actually just passing through — I didn't come here for the conversation. Well, not this one at least.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: What do you mean? What topic of conversation could be more sacred among scholars than the exploration of differing philosophies?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Well, based on what I've learned, Sachin and his "disturbing way of doing things" — as you put it — is very likely to have met your father twenty years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...What did you say?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Wait, so... No, surely that doesn't mean...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Hah. So that's why he thought I looked familiar. My father must've gone into the desert due to his influence...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I'm afraid so.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Good thing I shattered that diadem. From now on... nothing like that will ever have to happen again.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The boundaries of knowledge are ever-expanding. Someone else will inevitably pick up the same line of research one day, and Vahumana regards it as a reasonable research direction.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Oh, not this again... Even if you're right, and people are bound to fall into the same intellectual traps, things won't necessarily go the same way again next time.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You have to admit that the actions of one individual don't always predict the behavior of the group, and vice-versa. Take Sachin, for instance. He's quite an anomaly.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: And so is the one who stopped him — you. Conflicts of this nature are indeed exceptional, but it will occur again in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You said it yourself — the actions of one individual cannot predict the behavior of a whole group. You know that not everyone would have chosen as you did.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Even so, I stand by my views. You can forget about trying to convince me.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: That's fine. We've been arguing over this for years, and I don't hold any hope of you understanding. The issue we're debating has long since moved on from who's right and who's wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Thanks for letting me know all this.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: What?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I said, thanks for letting me know. Hey! Stop acting like you didn't hear me! You're doing this on purpose, aren't you!?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: They say that earnest thanks should be given thrice, so... One more time, please.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Well, how did it go? I assume that Lord Sangemah Bay's assistance helped you discover something, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Sachin was not a good person, and there's definitely something wrong with that Diadem of Knowledge!

choices.text: Indeed.

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Then in that case, shouldn't you be doing something about it?

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: For instance, telling the Akademiya that they should give up the Diadem—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We already told the Akademiya, but...

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: But what?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Kaveh smashed the diadem.

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Whaaaaat!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Calm down, Dori! Why are you getting so worked up?

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: My diadem... My beautiful diadem...

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Ah, this was supposed to be the perfect plan! I feed you the information, you discover the issue with the diadem, and then I just wait until the Akademiya sells it off at a low price...

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: And now it was all for nothing! Grr, curse that Kaveh! The interest rate on the Mora he owes me is about to get much higher!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohhh, so that's why you told us about this. Yeah, Paimon did think you were being unusually generous...

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: My diadem! Ugh, I'm furious! That's it, no extension on his payment this month, no matter what reason he gives!

choices.text: We also discovered that.

dialogues.speaker: Nizam
dialogues.text: Hello, I am the Vizier. Do you need any help?

dialogues.speaker: Nizam
dialogues.text: If you wished to see the Interdarshan Championship, then unfortunately, the portion taking part in Sumeru City has concluded.

dialogues.speaker: Nizam
dialogues.text: ...Hold on, on closer inspection you seem to be that guest commentator.

dialogues.speaker: Nizam
dialogues.text: My apologies. I thank you for the contributions you made to the Akademiya Extravaganza. It's all thanks to your help that the first round concluded so smoothly.

dialogues.speaker: Nizam
dialogues.text: But I might have been overindulgent in my praise. I heard the Interdarshan Championship has also encountered similar difficulties before... This time, both the contestants and viewers have been spared any harm. How fortunate.

dialogues.speaker: Feresht
dialogues.text: Greetings. You may call me "Master Treasure Appraiser, Prospective Antiques Collector, and Future Prominent Businessman Feresht."

dialogues.speaker: Feresht
dialogues.text: Have you heard? The Akademiya is hosting some kind of celebration along with a competition. Supposedly, the champion's prize is an extremely rare treasure.

dialogues.speaker: Feresht
dialogues.text: I think it was called... the diadem of... something. Ah. It doesn't matter. The first trick to being an expert appraiser of treasures is to avoid getting intimidated by a treasure's name!

dialogues.speaker: Feresht
dialogues.text: In terms of appraising antique collections, I'm only slightly less refined than my father. If you want to know how much a certain treasure is worth, just bring it to me and I'll let you know after a glance.

dialogues.speaker: Rukh Shah
dialogues.text: It's not often that the Akademiya hosts an event like this. We need to increase the number of patrols inside the city for this special occasion.

dialogues.speaker: Rukh Shah
dialogues.text: This isn't even especially for the competition. In fact, it is the increase in tourists that require us to take additional care.

dialogues.speaker: Rukh Shah
dialogues.text: There are no shortage of devious people who are willing to take advantage of these festivities to mask their own nefarious deeds.

dialogues.speaker: Yavanani
dialogues.text: ...Should you deny that the Championship rates Darshans based on their scores, please recall that we all entered our respective Darshans via our test scores.

dialogues.speaker: Yavanani
dialogues.text: To overlook the scores is to overlook the very basis for all assessments made by the Darshans.

dialogues.speaker: Khaldun
dialogues.text: In turn, you should remember before you overemphasize the scores, that they are only representative of how each contestant performs for specific tasks exclusive to the competition.

dialogues.speaker: Khaldun
dialogues.text: Moreover, we also need to consider other probabilistic factors such as weather, geography, morale and so on.

dialogues.speaker: Yavanani
dialogues.text: Oh? And we didn't need to consider this when we were testing into our Darshans?

dialogues.speaker: Khaldun
dialogues.text: A sophistic comparison! My test scores can represent my capabilities, but it does not showcase the totality of what a Darshan represents.

dialogues.speaker: Khaldun
dialogues.text: A foolish opinion as usual. No offense intended.

dialogues.speaker: Yavanani
dialogues.text: Disagree though you may, scores determine the rankings and results speak for everything.

dialogues.speaker: Homayun
dialogues.text: Even if we find a calm place to think, we will inevitably be interrupted by noisy students.

dialogues.speaker: Homayun
dialogues.text: To be honest, I was never interested in these celebratory events or competitions when I was in the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Homayun
dialogues.text: Winning the Championship doesn't really help add any credit to your research, and any renown gained from it only amounts to some short-lived attention.

dialogues.speaker: Homayun
dialogues.text: ...Realistically speaking, there are few people as practical as I am.

dialogues.speaker: Farghani
dialogues.text: Star... star course deviations...

dialogues.speaker: Farghani
dialogues.text: Ah, if I continue my studies down this path, I might just be able to see why there is a separation between my theories and the calculations.

dialogues.speaker: Farghani
dialogues.text: The Interdarshan Championships have done a lot of good this time. If Rtawahist hadn't selected Miss Layla as the representative, I would have never consulted her research.

dialogues.speaker: Farghani
dialogues.text: I can only say that Miss Layla keeps too low a profile. Such incredible research needs to be seen by more people.

dialogues.speaker: Shatir
dialogues.text: A pity that knowledge so great is constrained by matters of Mora...

dialogues.speaker: Shatir
dialogues.text: And when there are wealthy sponsors, the wealth is not fed into valuable research but rather burned on frivolous competitions...

dialogues.speaker: Shatir
dialogues.text: You mean the sponsor? Hm... I haven't heard much about them, but they should be a good person.

dialogues.speaker: Shatir
dialogues.text: Even merchants who think of nothing but profit should not be judged with prejudice so long as they are willing to place emphasis on the development and preservation of knowledge.

dialogues.speaker: Shatir
dialogues.text: ...Because, when it comes down to it, almost anything is better than someone who wastes money.

dialogues.speaker: Makhfi
dialogues.text: I didn't expect Tighnari, who rarely shows himself in the city, to participate in the Interdarshan Championship.

dialogues.speaker: Makhfi
dialogues.text: I don't know much about Tighnari. He doesn't strike me as someone who is fame-hungry... Perhaps too many people were recommending him, and he didn't want to disappoint them.

dialogues.speaker: Makhfi
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, I think he's planning to hold a new lecture next month.

dialogues.speaker: Makhfi
dialogues.text: I must note down the time of his lecture before I forget... I can't miss it!

dialogues.speaker: Arina
dialogues.text: I want a break... Why can't the Akademiya give us some time off during the Extravaganza?

dialogues.speaker: Armin
dialogues.text: Don't you enjoy watching the competition?

dialogues.speaker: Arina
dialogues.text: No, I do but... If you think about it, we can only watch the competitions if we have a break, right?

dialogues.speaker: Armin
dialogues.text: Yeah, that makes sense... Though, watching all my senior classmates represent their Darshans has inadvertently inspired a new drive in me to study!

dialogues.speaker: Armin
dialogues.text: I've made up my mind. In the future, I'm going to enter the Interdarshan Championship too!

dialogues.speaker: Arina
dialogues.text: Huh... It's a bit early to be thinking about this, isn't it? Didn't our instructors say that seeking knowledge should be a steady and serious endeavor?

dialogues.speaker: Arina
dialogues.text: Maybe before considering partaking in a competition that happens once in a blue moon, maybe you should consider which Darshan you want to join first?

dialogues.speaker: Ashk
dialogues.text: It's said that you can see pretty far if you stand high, but the higher you go, the harder it is to see what's right beneath you...

dialogues.speaker: Ashk
dialogues.text: Ah, sorry. I was talking to myself.

dialogues.speaker: Ashk
dialogues.text: If you're looking to join the Akademiya Extravaganza, then you probably got lost to wander this far. You're way past the boundaries of the festivities.

dialogues.speaker: Hunayn
dialogues.text: Huh? I didn't think someone would want to chat with me even now. Aren't you joining in on the Akademiya Extravaganza?

dialogues.speaker: Hunayn
dialogues.text: Hmm... What fun events are there... Truth be told, I'm not one for such occasions, so I can't say.

dialogues.speaker: Hunayn
dialogues.text: However, I don't dislike these celebratory events. The more students join in such galas, the quieter things are over here.

dialogues.speaker: Shohre
dialogues.text: Hello, what do you need?

dialogues.speaker: Shohre
dialogues.text: Oh? So you don't exactly know what I do, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Shohre
dialogues.text: No worries. As a matter of fact, that's a good thing. The fewer people who come to talk to me about work, the better — that means our academic environment is a healthy one.

dialogues.speaker: Shohre
dialogues.text: Honestly, I expected a great deal of problems to follow the Akademiya's celebration. I was even ready to head back to the office and prepare for overtime.

dialogues.speaker: Shohre
dialogues.text: But there really haven't been that many people seeking me out. Even the General Mahamatra is on break... Hm. I'm just going to keep resting here.

dialogues.speaker: Erfan
dialogues.text: What a blunder... I won't get to watch the competitions during the day if I'm working nights!

dialogues.speaker: Erfan
dialogues.text: That said... ah, I can't just dip work and go see the competition during the day, haha.

dialogues.speaker: Erfan
dialogues.text: Keeping that in mind gives me some balance. Maybe my classmates might fill me in on what's happening in the competition over some drinks at night.

dialogues.speaker: Erfan
dialogues.text: With the gala comes more tourists, and with more tourists comes an increase to my pay. I might even hear some new drunken jokes! Seems like I'm being well compensated for my time!

dialogues.speaker: Farhad
dialogues.text: Though work is as boring as ever and Zubayr Theater has no new showings, there seems to be no shortage of prospects as of late!

dialogues.speaker: Farhad
dialogues.text: Say, friend, are you going to watch the Interdarshan Championship? I hear Miss Nilou's going to be commentating!

dialogues.speaker: Farhad
dialogues.text: I wasn't much of a student growing up. Felt like I had an allergy to learning. However, after listening to how Miss Nilou breaks things down, the knowledge seems a lot easier for me to grasp.

dialogues.speaker: Farhad
dialogues.text: If you missed Miss Nilou's commentary, it's your loss.

choices.text: I'll give it a go.

choices.text: I'd like to give this a try.

choices.text: I've got other things to do right now, sorry.

choices.text: I'll give this one a go, why not?
